results.title: MOEMS and Miniaturized Systems XXV, Conference Details
results.content: Highly miniaturized optical and photonic systems are at the heart of an exceptionally broad spectrum of applications and coalesce a rich expanse of diverse technologies into components and assemblies with high functionality yet very compact dimensions. We invite papers related to miniaturized optical systems spanning all relevant technologies, from micro-optics to silicon photonics. The conference provides a forum for the presentation of new and exciting research on materials and fabrication, particularly novel and unconventional fabrication processes; hybrid and heterogeneous integration techniques, including photonic assembly and packaging; and cutting-edge applications for hybrid, integrated and chip-based optical microsystems. We present functional 3D-printed glass optical devices, including on-chip ring resonators and photoluminescent sources, and fiber-tip refractive index sensors and polarization beam splitters, opening new avenues for high-performance optical microsystem integration. Highly-stable and compact immersion micro-optical system for robust photonic integration (Invited Paper). The micro-optical system is aligned and fabricated directly on a Photonic Chip surface using high precision Two-Photon-Polymerization (TPP) lithography and features an integrated fiber port and a protective enclosure which air seals the coupling optics ensuring high optical performance and long-term reliability.

results.title: AI and Optical Data Sciences VII, Conference Details
results.content: I will then highlight advances in AI and automation for photonic design, including physical AI-based Maxwell solvers, fabrication-aware inverse design framework, MAPS, and scalable inverse training algorithm of meta-optical neural networks. We present a unified photonic processing platform that, based on III-V semiconductors, combines linear circuit reconfigurability with programmable nonlinear optical functions, enabling compact, adaptive optical computing. These diffractive processors designed by deep learning have various applications, e.g., all-optical image analysis, feature detection, object classification, computational imaging and seeing through diffusers, also enabling task-specific camera designs and new optical components for spatial, spectral and temporal beam shaping and spatially-controlled wavelength division multiplexing. We demonstrate the efficiency of linear programmable photonic neural networks for low-power optical computing applications. By generating hypervectors with over 100,000 dimensions through optical scattering and integrating them with holographic memory-based computing, we achieve significant improvements in latency and energy consumption compared to electronic and photonic neural networks.

results.title: Integrated Optics: Devices, Materials, and Technologies XXX
results.content: In this paper, recent development on the InP membrane nanophotonics technology will be reviewed, with a focus on novel material integration to achieve new functionalities, such as high speed modulation, optical circulator, optical memory as well as photonic neural network. We have recently shown that in addition to being excellent materials for bulk optic applications such as windows and lenses, CHIPs are excellent materials for integrated photonics, as their high refractive indices provide for compact components such as microring resonators, while their low losses enable high levels of integration. The demonstrated second-order nonlinear optical performance on a wafer-scale, CMOS-compatible AlN photonics platform highlights its strong potential for integrated frequency-comb generation and applications in AR/VR, biosensing, and quantum photonics. Integration of efficient electro-optic phase shifters in the C-band on a low loss SiN platform will relax design and performance constraints on applications requiring many phase shifters, including optical phased arrays, photonic integrated channelizers, and dynamic polarization controllers.

results.title: Optical Interconnects and Packaging 2026
results.content: Ultra-low coupling loss between Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs) and optical fiber arrays is a fundamental requirement for enabling the disruptive potential of photonic quantum computing systems. Enabling scalable co-packaged optics through high-precision glass structuring and photonic integration on panel-level substrates (Invited Paper). CPO integrates photonic and electronic components within a single package, enabling high-bandwidth, low-power optical I/O directly adjacent to ASICs. However, designing optical I/O systems in CPO is challenging due to fiber-to-chip dimensional mismatches and tight alignment tolerances. A key hurdle to overcome for successful co-packaging of photonic integrated circuit (PIC) transceivers, is the development of a pluggable interconnect, which can successfully couple the light from the optical fiber network to the PIC. Efficient light coupling for fiber-to-fiber and fiber-to-chip connections is crucial for photonic applications, particularly with advancements in data communication and co-packaged optics (CPO). Efficiently coupling light into and out of photonic integrated circuits (PICs) and optical fibers has become a foundational challenge to enable fast and low latency data transfer.

This configuration enables real-time 3D imaging with improved speed, resolution, and robustness, making it suitable for high-precision applications in optical metrology and biomedical imaging. Calibration of the fiber interferometer yielded a free spectral range of 32.5 MHz (0.26 pm) and an absolute measurement error of 64 MHz. The system frequency resolution is 443 kHz.
